words.gloss: one who does not know / ignorant person

literal: Even if [the king] is one who does not know, having destroyed [his own] intellect, speaking beneficial advice is the duty of the one who is by his side.
translation: Even if the ruler has destroyed his own intellect and remains ignorant, it is the duty of the minister who stands by his side to offer sound, beneficial counsel.
modern: தன் அறிவை அழித்துக் கொண்டு ஒருவன் (அரசன்) நல்லவற்றை அறியாதவனாக இருந்தாலும், அவனது அருகில் இருக்கும் அமைச்சர் அவனுக்கு நன்மையான உறுதிமொழிகளைக் கூறுவது கடமையாகும்.
explanation: This couplet outlines the absolute duty of a minister or close advisor when dealing with an incompetent or stubborn leader. The phrase 'அறி கொன்று அறியான்' refers to a ruler who has ruined his own capacity to think and remains ignorant of what is right. The word 'எனினும்' (even if) emphasizes that the leader's ignorance is no excuse for the advisor's silence. The minister, referred to as 'உழையிருந்தான்' (the one who is by his side), must speak 'உறுதி' (firm, beneficial advice). The poet declares this to be an absolute 'கடன்' (duty), meaning the minister must perform it regardless of whether the ruler listens or gets angry.
